subject.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists

question: Should the access-request workflow be redesigned around canonical `accessGroups` with explicit content-bearing pre-auth activation, or should OpenClaw intentionally support fixed per-sender trust tiers and automatic trusted-hook activation as additional permanent contracts?
rationale: Implementation evidence cannot choose the permanent config/API model or accept the pre-admission privacy and upgrade-time activation changes; those require explicit product and security ownership.

options.title: Refactor To Canonical Groups
options.body: Retain the access-request workflow, use `accessGroups` and matched-group metadata, and require explicit opt-in before handlers receive blocked-message content.

options.title: Approve Parallel Trust Tiers
options.body: Accept the six fixed labels and grouped allowlist objects as a distinct contract with explicit compatibility, upgrade, privacy, and multi-account proof.

options.title: Split Or Pause
options.body: Separate the generic pre-auth hook from grouping and automatic access-request activation, or pause the broad proposal until each direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Refactor To Canonical Groups
recommendation.body: Retain the access-request workflow, use `accessGroups` and matched-group metadata, and require explicit opt-in before handlers receive blocked-message content.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to the shared ingress, allowlist, config-mutation, and plugin SDK decision surface.
